He describes a game-playing agent called Simma, which can directly take control and play existing computer games with varying levels of success. 

Simma can be placed inside Genie 3, meaning one AI is deciding actions while another AI generates the game world in real time. Simma can be given goals, such as finding a key in a room, and will send commands as if playing a regular game, but the environment is produced on the fly by Genie 3. 

This setup could be valuable for generating unlimited training data, which would be useful for robotics and for training general AGI systems.

This short episode is from a talk given by Peter D. Kaufman on the multidisciplinary approach to thinking. 

Peter has one of the best track records in business history, but prefers to stay out of the spotlight. 

There is a simple takeaway. 

Using a multidisciplinary understanding of things, Peter identifies two often overlooked, parabolic “Big Ideas”: 

1. Mirrored Reciprocation (go positive and go first); and 

2. Compound Interest (constant progress over a long time)

A great “Life Hack” is to simply combine these two into one basic approach to living your life:

There may be no better formula for living the best life you could possibly live.
